source_text: Plane nativitas a Gabriele adnuntiatur. Quid illi cum angelo creatoris? Et in virginis uterum conceptus inducitur. Quid illi cum Esaia propheta creatoris? Odit moras, qui subito Christum de caelo deferebat. Aufer hinc, inquit, molestos semper Caesaris census et diversoria angusta. et sordidos pannos et dura praesepia. Viderit angelica multitudo dominum suum noctibus honorans. Servent potius pecora pastores; et magi ne fatigentur de loginquo; dono illis aurum suum. Melior sit et Herodes, ne Hieremias glorietur. Sed nec circumcidatur infans, ne doleat, nec ad templum deferatur, ne parentes suos oneret sumptu oblationis, nec in manus tradatur Simeoni, ne senex moriturus exinde contristetur. Taceat et anus illa, ne fascinet puerum. His, opinor, consiliis tot originalia instrumenta Christi delere, Marcion, ausus es, ne caro eius probaretur. Ex quo, oro te? Exhibe auctoritatem. Si propheta es, praenuntia aliquid: si apostolus, praedica publice: si spostolicus, cum apostolis senti: si tantum Christianus es, crede quod traditum est: si nihil istorum es, merito dixerim, morere. Nam et mortuus es, qui non es Christianus, non credendo quod creditum Christianos facit, et eo magis mortuus es quo magis non es Christianus, qui cum fuisses, excidisti, rescindendo quod retro credidisti, sicut et ipse confiteris in quadam epistula et tui non negant et nostri probant. Igitur rescindens quod credidisti iam non credens rescidisti, non tamen quia credere desisti, recto rescidisti, atquin rescindendo quod credidisti probas ante quam rescinderes aliter fuisse. Quod credidisti aliter, illud ita erat traditum. Porro quod traditum erat, id erat veru, ut ab eis traditum quorum fuit tradere. Ergo quod erat traditum resciodens quod erat verum rescidisti. Nullo iure fecisti. Sed plenius eiusmodi praescriptionibus adversus omnes haereses alibi iam usi sumus. Post quas nunc ex abundanti retractamus, desiderantes rationem qua non putaveris natum esse Christum.
orientation: Tertullian is addressing Marcion directly, charging that Marcion cut out all the Gospel accounts of Christ's birth because they proved his flesh was real.
pass_a_gloss: Plainly [the] birth by Gabriel is announced. What [is it] to him with [the] angel of the creator? And into [the] womb of [the] virgin [the] conception is introduced. What [is it] to him with Isaiah [the] prophet of the creator? He hates delays, [he] who suddenly Christ from heaven was bringing down. Take away from here, he says, [the] troublesome always censuses of Caesar and [the] narrow lodgings and [the] dirty rags and [the] hard mangers. Let [the] angelic multitude have seen its lord by nights honoring [him]. Let [the] shepherds rather keep [the] cattle; and [the] magi let [them] not be wearied from afar; give [back] to them their gold. Let Herod also be better, lest Jeremiah glory. But neither let [the] infant be circumcised, lest he feel pain, nor let [him] be carried to [the] temple, lest he burden his parents with [the] cost of [the] offering, nor let [him] be handed into [the] hands of Simeon, lest [the] old man about to die from then on be saddened. Let that old woman also be silent, lest she bewitch [the] boy. With these, I think, counsels all [the] original documents of Christ to delete, Marcion, you have dared, lest his flesh be proved. From what, I ask you? Show [your] authority. If [you are] a prophet, foretell something: if [you are] an apostle, preach publicly: if [you are] an apostolic [man], think with [the] apostles: if [you are] only a Christian, believe what has been handed down: if you are none of these, rightly I would say, die. For you are dead also, [you] who are not a Christian, by not believing what believed makes Christians, and by that the more you are dead by how much the more you are not a Christian, [you] who, when you had been [one], fell away, by cutting away what you had previously believed, just as you yourself confess in a certain letter and your [followers] do not deny and our [people] prove. Therefore cutting away what you had believed, now not believing, you have cut [it] away, not however because you ceased to believe [that] you cut [it] away rightly, but rather by cutting away what you had believed you prove [that] before you cut [it] away it had been otherwise. What you had believed otherwise, that had been handed down so. Further, what had been handed down, that was true, as [it was] handed down by those whose [office] it was to hand [it] down. Therefore what had been handed down cutting away, what was true you cut away. By no right you did [it]. But more fully such prescriptions against all heresies elsewhere already we have used. After which now out of abundance we retract, desiring [the] reason by which you did not think Christ to have been born.

Imperative of morior; Tertullian's rhetorical command to Marcion.
Perfect of rescindo; Tertullian's repeated charge that Marcion cut away what he had believed.

pass_b_english: Gabriel announces the birth. What has his Christ to do with the Creator's angel? And the conception is brought into the virgin's womb. What has he to do with Isaiah, the Creator's prophet? Marcion hates delays, this man who was suddenly bringing Christ down from heaven. "Take away," he says, "those censuses of Caesar that are always such a nuisance, and the cramped lodgings, and the filthy rags, and the hard mangers. Let the angelic multitude see to honoring their Lord at night. Let the shepherds keep their cattle instead, and let the magi not weary themselves from afar; I give them back their gold. Let Herod be better too, so that Jeremiah may not boast. But let the infant not be circumcised, so he won't feel pain, and let him not be carried to the temple, so he won't burden his parents with the cost of the offering, and let him not be handed into Simeon's hands, so the old man about to die won't be saddened from then on. Let that old woman be silent too, so she won't bewitch the boy."

With these plans, I think, you dared, Marcion, to destroy all the original records of Christ, so that his flesh would not be proved. On what authority? Tell me. If you are a prophet, foretell something; if you are an apostle, preach publicly; if you are an apostolic man, think with the apostles; if you are merely a Christian, believe what has been handed down; if you are none of these, I would rightly say: die. For you are dead indeed, you who are not a Christian, by not believing what is believed to make Christians, and you are all the more dead the more you are not a Christian. You, having once been one, fell away by cutting away what you had previously believed, as you yourself confess in a certain letter, and your followers do not deny, and our people prove.

Therefore, by cutting away what you believed, you have cut it away no longer believing; yet not because you ceased to believe did you cut it away rightly. On the contrary, by cutting away what you believed, you prove that before you cut it away it was otherwise. What you believed as otherwise, that was what had been handed down. Moreover, what had been handed down was true, as handed down by those whose task it was to hand it down. Therefore, by cutting away what had been handed down, you cut away what was true. You did it with no right.

But I have already used such preliminary arguments more fully against all heresies elsewhere. After those, I now revisit this matter out of abundance, desiring the reason why you thought Christ was not born.

polish.changed: Clarified that the opening objections are Marcion speaking, named Gabriel and Marcion explicitly, broke the long argument into paragraphs at the turn of thought, and smoothed sentence order for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: Marcion, in order to deny the flesh of Christ, denied also his birth
notes.why: Marcion is called 'that man from Pontus' in section 6 without explanation.

notes.quote: Take away, he says, those censuses of Caesar
notes.why: Reader cannot tell if 'he' is Marcion or Tertullian speaking as Marcion.

last_rejected.why: Latin refers to tight taxes/duties, not lodgings.
last_rejected.ruling: diversoria means lodgings/inns; angusta = narrow/cramped. Translation is correct, not taxes.

problems.quote: What does Gabriel have to do with the Creator's angel?
problems.why: 'illi' is Marcion's Christ, not Gabriel. Gabriel is the Creator's angel. The English makes them two different beings.
problems.fix: What has his Christ to do with the Creator's angel?

problems.quote: What does that have to do with Isaiah, the Creator's prophet?
problems.source_quote: Quid illi cum Esaia propheta creatoris?
problems.why: 'illi' refers to Marcion's Christ, not to the conception. The question asks what Christ has to do with Isaiah.
problems.fix: What has he to do with Isaiah, the Creator's prophet?

last_rejected.quote: What has his Christ to do with the Creator's angel?
last_rejected.why: illi is the same person as the next Quid illi (Marcion), not 'his Christ'.
last_rejected.fix: What has he to do with the Creator's angel?
last_rejected.ruling: "Quid illi cum angelo creatoris?" — illi is Marcion's Christ in context; 'his Christ' is a faithful clarifying rendering, and the preceding 'Quid illi' is also the Christ.
